newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says strong sterling anti-inflationary.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says strong sterling anti-inflationary.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday the strong pound distorted Britain's trade with other countries but helped to counter inflationary pressures.

"The pound is getting very strong and it distorts our trade. It's very counter-infationary," he told BBC's Radio Four. Clarke said the pound had risen 15 percent in the last year overall, and was up 20 percent versus the mark. "That's very anti-inflationary," he said.

The outcome of Wednesday' meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George is expected around 0945 GMT, at the Bank's morning money market operations. Most analysts expect interest rates to remain on hold, despite calls from George for a rise.
Clarke refused to be drawn on interest rates, but said the strong pound would be one big factor he would consider.

"When I make decisions on interest rates I look at how good were conditions in shops for Christmas, what is happening to production, how strong is the housing market getting...The big thing at the moment is the pound is very strong and that is very anti-inflationary."
